items.title: Literal uniqueness gate cannot be passed by any positive-support candidate
items.detail: 17GEMSDOE E-proba-multiscale (sha256 ab0a0a62eecf066a82713b09dd49f0f638a91fa3dd81f54cc34ae89afa3872be, fetched from github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/17GEMSDOE docs/downloads/17GEMSDOE_E-proba-multiscale_20260930T044527Z.tif) has finite>0 on 5,167,373 of 5,167,373 footprint cells and 0 outside. Under the inherited rule (dots = finite>0), every nonempty candidate has 3-px overlap 1.0 > 0.70. The rule must be ruled on by the owner; no exemption was applied.
items.source: evidence/uniqueness_saturation_certificate.json; this session re-fetched the witness and checked coverage

items.title: Bridged sample_submission.tif is not the all-absence sample described on the official page
items.detail: data/official/sample_submission.tif has 60,988 cells equal to 1 (footprint 5,167,373), exactly the known-fault positives in labels.tif. The official problem page says the sample predicts total fault absence. The bridged file is used only for grid and footprint compatibility.

items.title: Downloadable TIFF fills outside the footprint with 0, not NaN
items.detail: The official rules say data outside the bounds is null or nan; the bridged template uses NaN outside the footprint. docs/downloads TIFF has 0 NaN and 9,564,337 zeros. Zero probability adds nothing to the TP/FP/FN terms, so scoring is unaffected, but the convention differs. Ambiguous whether "bounds" means the raster or the study area; the template reading (NaN outside the study area) is the safer one.

items.title: Holdout collar makes near-trace truth unobservable
items.detail: In all 20 fold-arm receipts the nearest visible-to-withheld-truth distance is 3.1623 px (sqrt 10). The 3-px collar removes visible catalogue within 3 px of withheld truth (src/gems57/holdout.py lines 301-302). Consequences: the holdout cannot reward dots within about 3 px of a known trace, and it rewards deleting them by construction. This is exactly the regime the competition text says matters ("splays and parallel strands", thread 11536). Holdout gains for E1-E3 say nothing about near-trace dots.

items.title: labels.tif and existing_faults.tif are byte-identical
items.detail: Both bridged files have sha256 7ba308cc...4093 (425,830 B). That is plausible if the training labels are the known faults, but two official files are listed under different names. Official-origin identity is not verified; a fresh DrivenData download is needed for a receipt.

items.title: Evaluator source hash differs from the Session-5 receipt; numbers identical
items.detail: evidence/relay_bend_holdout.json records evaluate_holdout.py sha256 90ec4a7a...55; HEAD has ad86640b...03. Git history for this file is squashed to one commit, so the difference cannot be diffed. Reproduction with the current file reproduces all 20 fold-arm rows and all 5 pooled binary and soft scores with zero numeric differences (evidence/session7_reproduction_compare.json). The receipt should be regenerated or annotated.

items.title: Brief says 0.3195 is the highest score; the public board says otherwise
items.detail: DrivenData public leaderboard (fetched 2026-10-10): #1 xiaofanhu 0.3774, #2 JerryDataWorks 0.3418, #8 DARD 0.3195, #22 extradr19 0.2778. 0.3195 is rank 8 on the public board. Board scores are public-split DW-Tversky, not private-test or final-round scores.

items.title: The 0.2778 public row is not linked to the GEMSDOE32 site
items.detail: The DrivenData public board shows 0.2778 for extradr19 (#22). The GEMSDOE32 site owner reports 0.2778 for its raster. The two are not linked by any receipt. Do not attribute the board row to the site.

items.title: Range error cause remains unproven
items.detail: The downloadable TIFF satisfies [0,1]: min 0.0, max 0.9014216, no NaN. No organizer receipt shows which file produced the reported "Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]" error. The fix is consistent with the official format (float32, [0,1]); it is not confirmed by the portal.
